class.name: SwimmingMode
class.description: Like [FlyingMode] the input is not flattened - you swim in whatever direction you point. Unlike it, gravity is not gone: it is scaled by [member WaterVolume.buoyancy] and by how much of the character is under the surface, so at neutral buoyancy a character at the waterline sinks until it is submerged and then hangs there. Floating up is a buoyancy above 1. A rise near the surface is damped by the immersion depth, and the lift half of a stroke is scaled by that same depth, because there is nothing to push against above the waterline. Between them a character holding [i]up[/i] treads water at the surface instead of launching out of it and arcing back in. Getting out of the water is therefore the jump's job. Taking it adds [member CharacterMovementComponent.out_of_water_jump_velocity] and hands over to [code]Falling[/code] in the same tick, which is what Unreal does with its [code]OutofWaterZ[/code] and for the same reason: the swim speed cap and the surface damping would both brake the impulse straight back down.
